description: How the customer roles of the transport network relate to each other: who contracts whom, who executes for whom, how money settles, and which feedback loops close the network.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Contracting and awarding of transport capacity

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Day-to-day planning, tendering, and execution of loads

relations.name: Sets strategy and routing guides
relations.description: Hands the yearly carrier strategy, negotiated rate cards, and routing guides to plant and DC planners as the operating frame for daily planning.

relations.name: Awards contract lanes
relations.description: Runs RFPs and awards yearly lane contracts and rate cards to mid-size carriers through freight procurement.

relations.name: Contracts forwarders for complex lanes
relations.description: Awards multi-leg, cross-border, and consolidation-heavy lanes to freight forwarders where a single asset carrier cannot cover the requirement.

relations.name: Tenders daily loads
relations.description: Tenders planned loads to contracted carriers down the routing-guide waterfall and receives acceptances, rejections, and status updates back.

relations.name: Hands off overflow and groupage
relations.description: Passes loads that need consolidation or short-notice cover to forwarders when the contracted waterfall is exhausted.

relations.name: Subcontracts client freight
relations.description: Covers client loads by subcontracting vetted trucking companies found through the freight exchange.

relations.name: Books spot capacity
relations.description: Books owner-operators for single legs and return loads posted on the exchange, often same-day.

relations.name: Subcontracts overflow loads
relations.description: Passes overflow or imbalanced legs to owner-operators to protect contract service levels without adding own fleet.

relations.name: Books dock slots
relations.description: Books loading and unloading slots for planned trips; drivers check in against the booked slot on site.

relations.name: Arrives against booked slots
relations.description: Arrives at plant and DC docks for loading and unloading according to the slot windows booked for the leg.

relations.name: Aligns load plan with site capacity
relations.description: Aligns the daily load plan with dock and yard capacity so tendered loads land in feasible slot windows.

relations.name: Settles through self-billing
relations.description: Settles executed transport through self-billing and freight audit against contracted rates, disputing deviations where needed.

relations.name: Pays spot legs under payment guarantee
relations.description: Pays owner-operators for subcontracted legs, backed by exchange payment guarantees that protect small carriers from non-payment.

relations.name: Feeds back turnaround performance
relations.description: Reports slot adherence and truck turnaround performance so planners adjust pickup windows and lane schedules.
